title: Enterprise Onboarding + Escalation + Integration + QBR Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the standard operating procedures we use for enterprise customer onboarding, integration verification, support escalation, known-issues triage, and quarterly business review (QBR) preparation. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and on-call SREs who support enterprise accounts.

Goals
- Onboard enterprise customers in a predictable, low-friction way that ensures production readiness.
- Verify integrations and model routing policies before go-live.
- Provide a clear, time-bound escalation path for incidents.
- Maintain an up-to-date catalogue of known issues and workarounds.
- Deliver QBR-ready health and usage reports with actionable recommendations.

Owners & Roles
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (owner_team)
- Primary CSM: assigned per account
- SE (Integration Lead): responsible for API connectivity, authentication, and sample workloads
- Support Engineering on-call: triage and bug replication
- Eng SRE: escalation for platform incidents and capacity degradations

Onboarding checklist (Pre-launch)
1. Account setup (CSM)
   - Confirm legal and billing sign-off.
   - Create organization in Redwood Console and assign team seats.
2. Security & Network (SE / Customer IT)
   - Exchange IP allowlist ranges or configure VPC peering.
   - Validate KMS/HSM integration if requested.
3. Authentication & Keys (SE)
   - Provide API key and scoped credentials.
   - Verify token rotation process and document secrets policy.
4. Test prompts & dataset (Customer + SE)
   - Collect representative prompt sets for latency and quality checks.
   - Provide sample medium-sized payloads and peak QPS expectations.
5. Capacity & Performance (SRE + Product)
   - Map expected peak QPS to Dedicated pool sizing recommendation.
   - Agree on SLO targets: e.g., P95 latency < 420ms for 32-token responses on hosted small models, error rate < 0.5%.
6. Integration smoke tests (SE)
   - Validate: authentication, model selection, streaming response, tool-calling (if applicable), and embeddings endpoint.
   - Run automated integration tests and capture results.

Integration Verification Guide
- Recommended API smoke tests (cURL examples):
  - Authentication + basic generate:
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"model":"redwood-llm-1", "input":"Hello world"}'

- Embeddings check:
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
    -d '{"model":"embed-small-v1", "input":"test"}'

- Streaming behavior validation: ensure client handles chunked transfer and reconnects with resume token when applicable.
- Schema & structured output: provide example JSON schema for model outputs when customers use structured responses or function-calling.

Integration Acceptance Criteria
- All smoke tests pass in staging environment.
- Sample prompts produce expected qualitative outputs for the provided evaluation set (CSM/SE review).
- Performance targets met for the provided sample load: latency, error rate, and cost projection signoff.
- Security checklist completed and documented.

Escalation Playbook (Support)
- Severity definitions:
  - Sev1 (Critical): Production outage affecting >20% of requests or major data loss. Target response: 15 minutes.
  - Sev2 (High): Significant degradation (latency or errors) affecting a critical path for customers. Target response: 1 hour.
  - Sev3 (Medium): Functional issues with workarounds available. Target response: 4 business hours.
  - Sev4 (Low): Cosmetic or backlog feature requests. Target response: next business day.

Escalation steps (ordered):
1. Triage (Support Engineer)
   - Reproduce and collect logs, request_id, org_id, model, route, input sample, timestamps.
   - Capture P95/P99 latency and error spikes from Console dashboards.
2. Notify (via Slack and PagerDuty)
   - Use channel: #cust-{org-shortname}-incidents for customer-facing comms.
   - PagerDuty escalation to Support oncall -> SRE -> Runtime oncall if platform-level.
3. Containment (Support + SRE)
   - If a degraded model variant is available, perform automated fallback to compatible variant (per routing policy).
   - Apply rate-limits or temporary throttling to keep system stable.
4. Root cause analysis & fix (Engineering)
   - Open an internal ticket with severity label and link to incident page.
   - If bug/rollout issue, coordinate hotfix or rollback using release runbook.
5. Customer communication (CSM)
   - Provide status updates at predefined cadences: 15m, 1h, 4h, and then every 24h until resolved for Sev1.

Contact matrix (primary):
- Customer Success: csm-team@redwood.ai
- Support PagerDuty: support-oncall (link in Console)
- SRE oncall: sre-oncall@redwood.ai
- Runtime/Serving team: runtime-oncall@redwood.ai

Known Issues & Workarounds (living table)
| Issue ID | Symptom | Workaround | Owner | Target fix ETA |
|----------|---------|------------|-------|----------------|
| KW-2026-01 | Streaming disconnects for some EU customers behind corporate proxies | Advise client to enable chunked transfer and increase socket timeout to 90s; escalate to Eng if persistent | SE | 2026-05-01 |
| KW-2026-02 | Occasional higher P95 on long-context requests (>2k tokens) | Recommend model-specific quantization profile and increase dedicated pool size; apply KV-cache hints | Runtime Team | 2026-04-15 |

When adding an entry: include precise reproduction steps, customer impact classification, related logs, and a short mitigation that Support can apply immediately.

Support process: ticket lifecycle
- Ticket creation: via Console support button, email, or partner portal. Capture required fields: org_id, route_id, example input, sample request_id, prowler logs, and SLA tier.
- Initial response SLA: Enterprise: 1 hour for P1/P2 during business hours.
- Triaged ticket: create internal JIRA if bug suspected, link incident page, and label with customer-impact.
- Resolution & verification: Support must verify fix in customer staging where possible before closing.
- Post-incident: schedule a postmortem for Sev1 incidents within 72 hours.

Health Checks & QBR Preparation
- Weekly health check (automated + manual) checklist:
  - Ingest: 7-day usage trends for tokens, embeddings, and routes.
  - Performance: P95 latency, error rate, and CPU/GPU utilization for Dedicated pools.
  - Cost: per-token unit cost trends and top 5 contributors to spend.
  - Quality: sample prompt set pass/fail and any quality regressions.
- QBR deliverables (CSM + SE):
  - Executive summary (1 slide): adoption, value delivered, and top risks.
  - Technical appendix: latency/cost charts, model versions in use, and any open engineering tickets.
  - Action items: prioritized list with owners and target dates.

QBR template (short)
1) Executive summary (1 page)
   - Adoption metrics: DAU, top routes, peak QPS, and monthly token consumption.
   - Business impact: examples of features enabled by Redwood.
2) Health & performance (2 pages)
   - Charts: 90-day trend for P95 latency and error rate.
   - Capacity: Dedicated pool utilization and headroom.
3) Open risks & action plan (1 page)
   - Outstanding integrations, planned rollouts, and required engineering work.

Operational tooling & dashboards to use
- Redwood Console: per-route latency, token cost breakdown, rollout status.
- Alerts: PagerDuty + Slack bridge for Sev1/Sev2 incidents.
- Internal dashboards: per-org SLI dashboards in Grafana (link in Console).

Templates & Artifacts
- Sample escalation email for Sev1 (CSM -> Customer):
  Subject: Incident update: service degradation impacting {org_name} (Incident #{incident_id})
  Body: We are actively investigating. Current status: {status}. Next update in 1 hour. Contact: {csm_email}.

- API integration test script (example): included as cURL in Integration Verification Guide above.
- QBR checklist (deliverables and owners): attach spreadsheets to each account page prior to meeting.

Maintenance & Review cadence
- Playbook review: quarterly by Customer Success with reviewers from SE and SRE.
- Known issues: review weekly and mark status: open / in_progress / resolved.
- Postmortems: link to incident postmortem and update known issues table if recurring.

Appendix: Quick runbooks
- Replicate latency spike
  1. Pull last 2 hours of request traces for org_id.
  2. Check model variant mix and routing fallbacks.
  3. Inspect Dedicated pool utilization and tail latency.

- Forced fallback to variant
  1. In Console, navigate to routing policy for org route.
  2. Set temporary policy: prefer "compatible-variant-vX" and disable autoscaling bursts.
  3. Monitor P95 for 15 minutes and confirm customer throughput recovers.

If you find gaps or outdated sections, submit an edit request on this page and assign to the playbook owner.
